# FFTW release snapshots

The files of the release archives of [FFTW](https://www.fftw.org/), one commit per release, exactly as published. This is not a fork and not a mirror. FFTW is developed and maintained by Matteo Frigo and Steven G. Johnson at https://www.fftw.org/ and https://github.com/FFTW/fftw3: nothing is developed or maintained here, and this repository is not affiliated with the project. It only keeps snapshots of the releases.

FFTW is a library for computing the discrete Fourier transform, written by Matteo Frigo and Steven G. Johnson (`AUTHORS`). It is under the GPL 2 or later (`COPYING`). Questions and contributions belong to the project: https://www.fftw.org/.

## Why this repository exists

[Jack Apps Collection for macOS](https://github.com/zinc75/jack-apps-collection-macos) builds FFTW and links it statically into its programs. Each program ships the licence and the source of the libraries it contains, so the collection needs to point to the exact source of the release that it uses. It does so with a Git submodule, which needs a commit of a Git repository.

The project has a Git repository, but it does not hold the source of a release: the codelets of the library are generated by `genfft`, written in OCaml, and are not committed there (the repository asks not to be checked out unless you know what you are doing). The release archive has them, and builds without OCaml. This repository gives that archive as a commit that a submodule can point to. The snapshots also keep the source available if the download site goes away.

## What is in it

Each tag points to a commit whose files are those of the release archive, nothing added and nothing changed. The commit message gives the address of the archive and its SHA-256, computed on the downloaded archive. The archive is also attached to the release of the same name.

The only addition is this `README`, in `.github/`, on top of the tagged commits: it is not part of any release.
